raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not want to spread myself too thin. On 4.1 mu, I will still keep a few crops, but I will do them in the way I know and can manage with family help. Cotton is still my main crop because I know it well and the land suits it. I will keep most land in cotton, leave a small piece in stevia for cash, and keep one small wheat plot that I follow with summer maize. That way, if one price is bad, I still have something else. I have a well, so I can save the crop if spring or summer turns dry, but pumping costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the field really needs it.

My schooling is low, so I do not count too finely. I look at what worked before, what my neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can safely spend. I will not cut fertilizer too hard because if the crop turns weak, the loss is bigger than saving a little money. But I also will not chase very high input because I am farming only 4.1 mu and some people in the house work outside, so labor at the right time matters more than fancy plans. On the wheat-maize piece, I will do quick turnover after wheat harvest, just one fast tillage pass and sow maize right away.
